title: Modification of Damon-Eshbach magnetostatic mode spectra in ferromagnet/paramagnet bilayer
abstract: Using the magnetostatic approximation, we calculate the spectra of bulk and surface spin waves in an in-plane magnetized ferromagnet/paramagnet bilayer. Due to the dipolar coupling between the layers, the paramagnet becomes polarized, which in turn modifies the spectrum of the Damon-Eshbach magnetostatic modes. We assume that the paramagnet is characterized by a magnetic susceptibility, $χ\propto 1/(T-T_C)$, which reaches large values when the system temperature $T$ is close to the Curie temperature $T_C$. We find the conditions under which surface spin waves become unidirectional, i.e., capable of carrying energy in only one direction, and determine the magnitude of their frequency nonreciprocity. We demonstrate the possibility of switching the unidirectional wave regime on and off by varying the external magnetic field or temperature, making the ferromagnet/paramagnet system an attractive platform for tunable magnonic logic devices.
summary: This theoretical study analyzes spin wave propagation in a ferromagnet/paramagnet bilayer using magnetostatic theory. The key finding is that dipolar coupling induces significant frequency nonreciprocity, enabling the creation of unidirectional magnonic waves. This tunability—switching these directional properties via temperature or magnetic field—suggests applications for novel magnonic logic devices.
main_problem: To calculate and analyze the spectra of Damon-Eshbach magnetostatic modes (surface and bulk spin waves) in a ferromagnet/paramagnet bilayer, focusing on how dipolar coupling modifies these spectra.
main_result: The dipolar coupling induces nonreciprocity in surface spin waves, allowing for the creation of unidirectional wave regimes that can be switched on or off by varying external magnetic fields or temperature near the Curie point.
method: Analytical calculation using the magnetostatic approximation and solving coupled differential equations across the FM/PM interface.
model_or_system: The system is an in-plane magnetized ferromagnet (FM) film placed on a paramagnet (PM) half-space. The PM's magnetic susceptibility follows the Curie-Weiss law, $\chi \propto 1/(T-T_C)$.
key_observables: Spin-wave frequency spectrum ($\Omega$), frequency nonreciprocity ($\Delta\Omega$), and group/phase velocities ($v_g, v_p$).
important_parameters: Magnetic permeability of the PM ($\mu$), external magnetic field ($H_0$ or $h$), and temperature ($T$) relative to the Curie temperature ($T_C$).
main_assumptions: The magnetostatic approximation is used, and the analysis assumes a thick FM film. The PM susceptibility follows the Curie-Weiss law.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of nonreciprocity ($\Delta\Omega$) on wave vector ($k$), showing unidirectional regimes; they also map out spectra for arbitrary propagation angles ($	heta$), revealing forbidden regions and mode splitting between MSSWs and BVMSWs.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the governing equations using magnetostatic theory, analyzes the specific case of perpendicular propagation ($k \perp M_0$) to show nonreciprocity, then extends the analysis to arbitrary propagation angles ($	heta$), detailing how MSSW and BVMSW spectra interact and defining parameter regimes for wave confinement.
why_interesting: While focused on magnonics rather than quantum information directly, the concept of tunable, directional energy transport (unidirectional waves) is analogous to engineered quantum channels or non-Hermitian physics studied in AMO/quantum optics.
